evidence.title: Community Banks Swing Back at Trump Regulators Over Crypto Charters

occurrences.quote_span: Under Gould, the OCC has granted preliminary approval to a slew of national trust charter applications by crypto companies that say they want to use the licenses to custody digital assets and issue stablecoins, a type of crypto designed to maintain a fixed value.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Independent Community Bankers of America

occurrences.checkable_against: ICBA complaint and federal court docket
occurrences.quote_span: The lawsuit asks a federal court in Washington, D.C. to vacate a rule that the regulator finalized earlier this year and guidance that the group said opened the door to the flood of applications for charters.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Independent Community Bankers of America

occurrences.quote_span: The OCC is responsible for chartering national banks and ensuring they remain financially stable.

occurrences.checkable_against: community bank statements and deposit and lending data
occurrences.quote_span: Smaller banks have been on edge that cryptocurrencies and stablecoins will draw deposits out of the banking system, which could reduce profits and their ability to lend.

occurrences.quote_span: The lawsuit by the Independent Community Bankers of America accuses the regulators of allowing “highly risky cryptocurrency and digital asset activities” to enter the banking system without submitting them to the same level of regulatory oversight as banks.

occurrences.quote_span: Trust banks traditionally don’t take deposits or make loans, meaning they aren’t subject to the same oversight or financial stability rules as other banks.

occurrences.quote_span: The lawsuit names the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and its head, Jonathan Gould.

occurrences.checkable_against: historical OCC national trust charter records
occurrences.quote_span: In the past, trust charters have been used by businesses such as insurance companies and payroll processors.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Independent Community Bankers of America

occurrences.quote_span: The ICBA in its lawsuit argues that the OCC has overstepped its statutory authority by expanding the types of activities that trust banks can engage in.
occurrences.speaker: Independent Community Bankers of America
occurrences.subject: Independent Community Bankers of America

occurrences.quote_span: The OCC’s actions “place community banks at a severe competitive disadvantage by allowing the national trust banks to offer many of the same services as community banks without complying with the same costly banking laws and regulations,” the ICBA said in its lawsuit.
